result:
Lowercase comparators like `like`, `ilike` and `is null` now work when searching experiments in the database-backed store, the same as their uppercase forms. The relevant tests pass.

**Cause:** the code that turns an experiment filter into SQL compared the comparator against uppercase strings only: `"LIKE"`, `"ILIKE"`, `"IS NULL"`, and so on. That code is `_get_search_experiments_filter_clauses` in `mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py`. The lower-level SQL helper it calls has the same uppercase-only checks. Run search already uppercases the comparator before doing either of these, which is why lowercase forms worked there.

**Fix:** a one-line change at `mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:9681`. The comparator is now uppercased (`f["comparator"].upper()`) before any checks run. That covers name and other attribute filters, `experiment_id` filters, and tag filters, including the `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` check on tags. Uppercase input is unchanged. When workspaces are enabled, experiment search goes through this same function, so it's fixed too.

**Tests:** your staged test, `test_search_experiments_filter_with_lowercase_comparator`, covers `name like`, `name ilike`, `tag.key like`, `tag.key ilike` and `tag.key is null`. All 10 of its cases pass, five with workspaces enabled and five without. The other 50 `search_experiments` tests in that file also pass. I didn't run anything outside that file.
